core_obligations: Finite separable case: use a primitive element and its minimal polynomial to exhibit a multiplicative subset of the square under which the multiplication map becomes a localisation (proof lines 10445-10460).

General case: write the extension as a filtered colimit of finite separable subextensions, note that every element of the kernel of multiplication is killed at a finite stage, and conclude by exactness of localisation (proof lines 10460-10471).
proof_roadmap: Do the finite separable case with a primitive element (proof lines 10445-10460).
Pass to the colimit and conclude by exactness (proof lines 10460-10472).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a separable algebraic extension the multiplication map on the square of the extension is obtained by inverting a multiplicative subset (statement lines 10437-10443). The proof handles the finite separable case through a primitive element and its separable minimal polynomial, then passes to the general case by writing the extension as a filtered colimit of finite separable subextensions and observing that every element of the kernel is killed at a finite stage, so that exactness of localisation finishes (proof lines 10445-10472). The reduction to finitely generated subextensions is the step that carries the general case. H2.
